messages.text: The new coastal studies are hung now. Several are quiet enough that they reward a second look, especially after a morning with figures.
The little brass fittings you showed me would look handsome beside the coastal drawings. Are you still keeping them on the back-room shelves?
Saturday at 11:20 should work. I will come after I reconcile the March assumptions and before I start correcting the footnotes.
For now. The half-rigged schooner is taking up the lower shelf, and the Florence notebook had to move beside the tall stack of exhibit catalogues.
That sounds very much like you: precise tools, old paper, and a small harbor tucked indoors.
That sounds like your usual sequence: measure, verify, then let the eye do its part.
The eye catches what the grid misses. I will bring the small notebook, not the laptop.
I found another packet from the old Norwich file cabinet: Dad's 2014 appointment cards, Mom's benefit statements, and those bank authorization forms you handled.
I found another envelope from the old Norwich dresser. It has Dad's shoe brush receipt tucked in with my eighth-grade immunization card.
Keep it in the blue folder for now. I remember spending half that winter on hold with the insurer and the branch manager.
Keep that envelope. The receipt may help date the small cedar box with his polish tins.
There is also a note from Mum about not leaving school bags in the front hall. That sounds exactly right.
You also wrote a note on the back: "Union St., 4:30, after probate copies." I assume that was one of your own appointments, not theirs.
It does. I can still picture your satchel by the radiator and my shoes lined under the bench.
Yes. Three visits, maybe four. It helped me sort the papers without snapping at everyone.
You see the harbor board clip making the rounds? Plenty of waving papers, no actual dock plan attached.
Saw it, then closed the tab. I am not feeding that comment thread.
Reasonable. The packet is on the town site if you want the dull version.
Dull version first. Facebook can keep the fireworks without me.
Weather looks tolerable Saturday if you have not used up all your civilized hours on last year's escapes.
I counted it last night: two Monday-Friday blocks, plus three Friday-Monday stretches. Saturday morning is clear.
Good. Bring the small Rome volume if you still want me to look at that bridge sketch.
It is on the east shelf in the back room with the Lisbon and Montreal ones. I will pull it after coffee.
I hung the small harbor interiors this morning. One of them has a ledger page worked into the paint, which made me think of your margin notes.
The south wall is finally hung. If you are in New London Saturday, stop by before the reception crowd arrives.
I can come through around 2:30. I saw the Wadsworth feed post a similar use of pale green this morning.
Saturday after lunch should work. I still have the museum essay you sent open beside a piece on municipal debt.
That pairing is very you. I will leave the catalog at the desk, and there is a short wall text on the old customs house.
Good eye. Bring that comparison with you; I would like to see whether it holds up in person.
Good. I may bring the notebook if the light in those rooms is as sharp as the installation photo.
The Saturday opening should be calm if you come early. The light in the harbor photographs is best before the room fills.
I may come after trimming the dill and basil boxes. If the wind stays down, I will walk the pier first and bring the small binoculars.
That sounds like your kind of sequence. I will set aside the catalog by the desk.
The gallery is quiet now, and your note about the C-major prelude stayed with me. You made it sound like architecture built out of restraint.
That one behaves like a room where every proportion has already been decided. I tried a little of it on the front-room instrument after supper.
I can imagine the old wood answering differently than a clean modern keyboard.
It answers slowly at first. Then the middle register opens up and words feel unnecessary.
I found the packet from Norwich City Hall in the estate folder. It has the 1962 certificate copy and the old Whitcomb notes tucked behind it.
Good. Keep that with the other papers for now. The clerk's seal may save me a second trip.
There is also a blank section on the benefits checklist asking for branch and discharge dates. I assume you want that left blank again.
Yes. The only old family line items I need are the Whitcomb side and Mother's McLeod page.
Club treasurer asked if you can sanity-check the reserve ladder before Saturday. I told him you still remember yield curves better than most people remember birthdays.
Send me the sheet. Those Storrs classes still pay for themselves in small, unglamorous ways.
Unglamorous is underrated. You would have hated being chained to that Manhattan desk you once mentioned.
The bonus looked good on paper. The Hartford client files looked like something I could still stand after ten winters.
Found a box of old winch manuals at the club. Half are missing dates. I assume this will offend your filing instincts.
Bring them Saturday. If the parts sheets have revision numbers, I can put them in order without guessing.
Of course you can. Did your father keep shop papers that way, or did you invent that affliction yourself?
He had binders for engine cards and pump service sheets. Mother used index cards and date stamps at her counter, so I was surrounded.
Found that old brass cleat in the garage. Looks like the sort your dad would have known by touch.
Likely. The smell of the rope locker came back before I even turned it over.
Bring it Saturday if you are heading down to the clubhouse. Martin will have an opinion, no doubt.
I am on the morning launch list, so I can show it to him after the 10:00 briefing.
Garden feed starts at 7:30. I have the radio on in the garage if Elaine lets me finish the shelf.
I will put NESN on after dinner. They have to stay out of the box tonight.
That and clear the front of the net. Same old story.
Send me your view after the first period. I am curious whether the pairings hold up.
I found another Norwich box. Mother kept the old meetinghouse programs with the Christmas cards, all perfectly readable, of course.
Save the programs. I remember the hymns more as family furniture than anything I ever kept up with.
That sounds about right. I will put them with the letters from Grandmother so Andrew does not need anyone to translate or explain the handwriting beyond our usual family scrawl.
Good. The family scrawl is burden enough.
Did you really make a tab for me after our rent talk? lol
I made a small one. Three columns: fixed bills, income swing, cash that should not be touched.
You and your columns. Still, send it. Providence keeps making the 'fixed' part a joke.
I'll send the clean copy after I finish my own 65 version. Mine has fewer surprises if I keep the hours capped.
Someone in my Providence group posted a whole screenshot storm about the spring booster schedule. Want me to forward it?
Send the original source if there is one. I will compare it with Dr. Hsu's portal note and the CDC table after lunch.
It is mostly comments and one cropped image, honestly.
Then I will skip it. The Yale New Haven page and the town notice matched each other last time, so that is enough homework for today.
That budget sheet you sent is almost annoyingly calm. Mine has rent screaming at the top.
Calm is easier when the fixed lines are few. February was 13,300 before the usual trims and about 8,000 actually reached the checking account.
So your advice is basically: keep the monthly claims on the account boring and don't make panic moves?
Boring helps. I also keep a separate bucket so a $400 repair doesn't become a drama.
Did you see the Providence ballot mailer? Half of them say build housing near rail, then dodge how to pay for the stations.
I put stars beside the ones who mention the bus lanes, the lead pipes, and a real bond schedule. Promises without a pay table make me nervous.
Very you. I figured you'd like the one pushing tenant vouchers and the port flood map disclosure.
Those both matter, but I still want someone who can read a balance sheet and not just win an argument online.
I found a small book of hillside facades from Liguria tucked behind the counter. The afternoon shadows on the shutters made me think of your pencil studies.
That sounds worth seeing. I have been collecting views where the houses are stacked tightly enough that the rooflines almost become steps.
Come by Saturday if you can. There are two plates with sea walls and terraces that might help your little coastal folder.
I will bring the gray notebook. The folder is getting more serious than I expected.
The small watercolors are hung now. If you come by after lunch tomorrow, the west wall has the quietest light.
That may be just right. I let the March renewal grid follow me past eleven last night and skipped the harbor loop this morning.
Then take the long route here and leave the grid closed until Monday. The paintings will tolerate a practical man looking slowly.
I will put the walk on the calendar first, then stop in. A half hour with color usually resets the machinery.
Are you still doing your first-Saturday papers this morning? I can call after lunch instead of interrupting.
That works. I am through Eversource and insurance, then Harborview drafts at 10:30. Laundry is already in.
Good. I wish Robert kept his folders that clean. Did the washer repair land in this month's total?
Yes. The sheet is sitting at $5,400 with that included, so I am leaving the extras alone until April.
Providence committee is arguing over whether the new crisis van should post monthly outcomes. You'd probably ask for columns before opinions.
Columns first, yes. Calls diverted, repeat calls, injuries, wait times, and what happens after six months.
They buried the camera complaint numbers in a PDF again. Classic.
A public table would settle more than a hundred speeches. Same with training hours and who reviews disputed footage.
Sent you that council clip from Providence. The stop-data chart starts around 18:20, if you want the non-shouty part.
Watched it with coffee. I put $30 toward the New London Rights Project afterward and printed the April sample sheet while the browser was open.
That is extremely Uncle Damon: one tab for public records, one tab for ballot logistics.
Also one tab for Mrs. Alvarez's missing 1099. Her bank site hides the useful button behind three menus.
Quick money question: when you get a one-off work payout, do you let yourself upgrade anything big right away?
Usually no. I let the standing pulls happen first, then send most of the extra check to the same few places: brokerage, HSA, and the house/car buckets.
So the apartment math stays based on normal pay, not the occasional spike?
Exactly. Normal pay covers normal commitments. The irregular money is mostly for shoring up the backstop or long-term accounts.
Random question: when you do open enrollment, do you actually compare the high-deductible option or just keep the same setup?
I compare the numbers, but usually keep the same setup. The payroll deduction has been predictable and the coverage works with my doctors.
Makes sense. My office keeps changing ours and everyone finds out by spreadsheet.
Mine is dull by comparison. I just need to submit the March confirmation and get back to the 8:00 budget call.
Quick question: if a city sends me five years of rent permits as a CSV, would you start in Sheets or just query it?
I would load it cleanly, check missing fields, then query the basic cuts before making any chart. The chart comes last.
That is less exciting than my plan, but probably why your work files do not explode.
Also write down what the data cannot answer. It saves trouble when someone wants a sharper answer than the file can support.
Before our four o'clock call, did you get outside today? Mystic is raw but not raining here.
Four still works for our call? Robert may be out in the garage, so I will keep him from interrupting unless the insurance envelope turns up.
Yes. The little clip-on said 7,680 when I came back, and I marked the gray sky beside the usual path.
Four works. I have the kettle set and the notebook on the table. Afterward I am keeping the evening plain and quiet.
Before our call, did you get your outside loop in today? It is raw here near Mystic.
That sounds sensible. Please do not push it if the wind comes up.
That sounds like you. I wanted to ask whether Andrew left the blue scarf in the spare room last week.
Shorter version. Down to the marina fence and back, fast enough to warm up.
Yes, folded on the chair. I will put it with the book I meant to mail him.
No heroics. I wrote it down and sat for ten minutes before taking the chair reading.
That sounds sensible. Keep writing down the morning cuff numbers, please.
I have. The last few are less stubborn, and the overnight chart is less chopped up.
Elaine says don't let her run past 4:40 today. I've got the folder from the cardiology office on the kitchen table.
Understood. I'll keep the call tight and ask only about the insurance pages she wanted me to check.
Good. If you drive down later this month, Mystic traffic is already acting like summer.
I'll avoid the bridge backups and bring the old Norwich envelope when I come.
Elaine says dinner at 6 next Sunday. I am making chicken, not the boxed rice mix.
That helps. I will bring a salad and skip the chips this time.
Good. You still doing that morning loop by the river?
Most days. I missed Friday because of the pharmacy stop, but the weekly average is intact.
I saw your comment under the battery-storage fund panel. Careful, Damon, the comments below those events get very certain very quickly.
I mostly saved it for the speaker list. One presenter had a useful slide on where automated scoring breaks down.
That sounds more like your sort of browsing than the gallery announcements I send you.
The gallery notices are still safer. I am copying only two figures from this one into my workbook, not the whole machinery.
Forecast has the gusts dropping by 1600. Club dock walk still looks tolerable, assuming the anemometer is not lying again.
That works. I can meet at the club at 4:30 and do the diner afterward, but I am leaving Wednesday evening empty.
Reasonable. The engine talk should be brief unless Carl discovers a new way to misuse a wrench.
If we end up at the counter, I may just have the soup and a glass of whatever red they keep open.
You free tonight? I can send the Providence housing spreadsheet after work, but no need to do uncle-level forensic accounting.
Send it, but I am setting a 45-minute block and stopping there. I ate over my keyboard yesterday and that is usually the sign to close the file.
Fair. Make the block, take the walk, then tell me if the rent assumptions are ridiculous.
That order works. I will put music on while I review it so I do not start inventing problems from 2028.
The rail map you sent is wild. Five stops that close together and still everyone argues about access and crowding.
That is part of the appeal. Compact towns, tight paths, no need for a car, and enough elevation to make every street corner look different.
You also circled the room rates like a bond analyst. September does look less punishing.
I am letting the separate account do its work before I pretend the dates are real.
Thanks for talking through the rent-versus-IRA thing. I was about to throw a screenshot into the group thread and make it everyone's problem.
Better handled in a call. Send me the numbers after work tomorrow and I will look quietly.
Will do. Providence rents are ridiculous again, so my patience is thin.
Thin patience is allowed. Bad arithmetic is not.
Uncle D, people are posting that zoning screenshot again. It leaves out the second page.
Then use the full packet in your reply. I would not chase every cousin-of-a-cousin thread.
Hard not to. The comments are a wreck.
Send one clean link if you must. I am leaving my page quiet tonight.
The architect from the March opening asked whether you still review small organizational problems over coffee.
Only if it stays small. I am keeping those conversations to Tuesday or Thursday mornings.
That sounds very much like you. I can say you prefer a contained first conversation.
Please do. I want notes and numbers before I agree to anything recurring.
Robert's neighbor insists the ginger tea and shoulder rubs are all he needs after Wednesday. I put the discharge folder on the kitchen table, but it made me second-guess myself.
I found a photograph of you by the Thames with your cuffs rolled up. Mum wrote 1968 on the back.
The tea and rubs are fine for comfort. Keep the folder as the guide, and ask the cardiology nurse about anything that does not match it.
That would be near the yard gate. I remember waiting there while Dad finished his shift.
That is what I needed to hear. I will not read the neighborhood replies tonight.
Good. I can drive over Tuesday if the 10:20 follow-up stays on the schedule.
I will save it for you. Are you still going to that Wednesday evening chart talk with Martin?
Yes, weather permitting. I promised to help stack chairs afterward.
Your model note was tidy. I still think you are giving the maintenance variable too much dignity.
Possibly. I kept the old number in the margin until I can justify the change from invoices, not mood.
Good. Bring it Friday if the wind stays reasonable. Also, leave room for one imperfect human sentence.
I added three lines after listening to the Takemitsu recording. Less chrome-plated now.
Wind looks useless Saturday. If we are postponing the club, are you doing your New London detour instead?
Possibly. Clara said the back room changed, and the Met posted a staircase detail that made me want to look at her lintel photographs again.
That is a very specific reason to cross the bridge. More disciplined than my excuse for diner pie.
The pie argument may still prevail if the rain arrives early.
Garage says Elaine's alternator is $386 before tax. Annoying timing.
If that were mine, I would just pull it from checking and top the reserve back up next deposit.
Good spot to be in. We still get too many monthly envelopes.
I worked hard to get rid of those. The car title and the old campus paperwork are both long filed away.
TV guy says the harbor grants are pork. Same guy wants the bridge fixed before tourist season.
A bridge inspection, sewage pump, and clinic roof are not luxuries. I care whether the bid is clean and the debt service is honest.
Fair. Elaine asked if that forwarded post about counting machines was junk.
Tell her I would wait for the registrar notice. The screenshot has no source line, and the dates do not match the town calendar.
Elaine says you may want the little Kiwi tin from the basement shelf. Still has the old brush inside.
Yes, please set it aside. That sat on the Norwich back-stair shelf for years.
Will do. Also found a framed photo: you in a blazer, Elaine much smaller, your folks on either side.
That should be the one from the front steps. The blazer was probably pressed twice before the picture.
Did you see the Providence bond explainer I sent? The comment section is already a mess.
I printed the actual notice instead. Easier to mark up, and it sits better next to the chapter I am on.
Of course you printed the notice. Also, was the book the one about the postwar ports or the one with the train stations?
Ports. I put a tab where the author compares harbor spending to school building campaigns.
The archival show opens tomorrow. One wall has photographs of white-steepled meetinghouses and town greens; I thought of your Norwich stories.
Those buildings were the backdrop to half our family errands, though not much more these days.
That distance may make your eye sharper. Bring any old family notes if you want; the curator likes seeing how plain domestic writing sits beside public architecture.
I have a few notes from home that Andrew could read without help. I may bring copies, not originals.
The installation photo came through beautifully. The lintel detail is sharper than I expected.
Good. I added it to the locked March page beside the municipal-bond paragraph and the Genoa alley sketch.
That is quite a pairing, though very much your way of seeing things.
The page is only for me, so the odd pairings can stay. I still need to check the old paper volume from the back room.
The maritime exhibit has a case of parish maps from Norfolk and the Fife coast. Your note about Whitcomb and McLeod records made me think of it.
That sounds worth seeing. The family sheets are dry reading, but the map context helps.
Saturday after the opening would work. Bring the Norwich copy if you want; old paper has a way of clarifying family stories.
I can bring a scan. The original needs to stay flat until the renewal envelope is done.
I woke up around twelve and saw your front room light from the street camera notification. Everything all right?
Yes, nothing wrong. I lost track after opening the small blue Henle book.
I am glad it was only that. Please remember the neighbors have ears, even if they are polite ones.
Point taken. The old bench will be occupied earlier tonight.
Robert says he saved the black-and-gold game for later, so we may call closer to 4:30 Sunday if that is all right.
That is fine. If there is overtime, tell him I will not spoil it.
Thank you. He is pretending he can ignore the score, but I know better.
Wind is marginal for the club dock this morning. Better walking weather than rigging weather.
Agreed. I will take the Avery Point path instead. The thyme needs thinning when I get back, and there is a chess diagram I have been avoiding.
That sounds more productive than watching people argue with halyards in a crosswind.
I will save the rigging lecture for next time.
Fog is lifting by ten. Not elegant, but serviceable for the waterfront stretch.
I may take the long way past Avery Point if the pavement dries. That usually lands just under four miles on the counter.
Check the gusts at the point. Engineers call that a boundary condition, walkers call it annoying.
I will add fog and gusts to the page. Resting number was 62 before coffee, so no excuse there.
If the tiny mast keeps leaning, check the jig before blaming the glue. Engineers have been unfairly accused for less.
The jig is square. The problem is that I keep measuring with the laptop open on one side and the old Steinway crowding my chair on the other.
Two screens, one keyboard, one piano, and miniature rigging. That room needs traffic control.
Agreed. I will move the pilot books before I put any more thread through those blocks.
Community center lot was half ice at 7. Use the side door if you go.
Thanks. I did twenty-five minutes inside instead of the river path.
Good. Elaine says your little notebook is looking better.
It is trending the right way. Also easier to stay asleep after those morning sessions.
Photo came through. That water stain looks old, not active. I would not let them sell you a full ceiling job.
Elaine found that old envelope from your Volvo stop. Was it one paper or two?
That matches what the plumber said. I put the small patch on April's list so March stops at the $5,400 mark.
Two total, both years ago. One on Route 2 and one near Colchester. Nothing worth saving except the dates.
She also had Mrs. Keane's broken-window note tucked in there. That one got a case number, at least.
Good. I only wanted the numbers because City Hall keeps saying the records are easy to compare.
Smart. Do the Saturday wash before you start sanding anything. Dust gets everywhere.
Exactly. Wash first, patch after lunch, then the freezer containers Sunday.
Elaine says the cardiology bill has two adjustment lines. You ever see that on your plan?
Yes. Mine posts the negotiated line first, then the patient share. Send me a photo of the page and I will look after I clear the approvals queue.
Will do. No rush. Sounds like you are still at it.
About another half hour. Fridays run long when the department heads wait until four.
Bruins are on at 7:30. You watching from your kitchen command post again?
Likely. Radio low, sink cleared, one bowl of chowder. Best way to keep the commentary sensible.
Elaine says you still keep the front room too neat for human use.
It works for me. When people come through, I know where everything goes back.
Found the old photo Mom had of you in the Norwich kitchen with a stack of textbooks. Wild that you were doing bond math at that table.
That table was where bills, homework, and tax forms all landed. It made the math feel less theoretical.
Makes sense why your advice is always boring in a useful way. Pay the loan, keep the reserve, ignore the shiny job title.
I have seen shiny titles come with a lease in Queens and no Sunday dinner nearby.
The opening starts at 4:30 today. I saved you the smaller catalogue; it will fit in your coat pocket.
Thank you. I am walking over after lunch if the rain holds, and I will eat before I arrive.
Wise. The reception table is mostly crackers, cheese, and those little cured meats.
Then I will admire them from a respectful distance. I also need to be home by 7 for the evening tablet.
The gallery table is set for Thursday. I also tucked aside the flyer from the courthouse intake group you asked about.
Thank you. I can come after I bring Mrs. Alvarez's envelope back upstairs; we found the pension statement.
Excellent. If you arrive before six, the League volunteers will still have their April packets by the front desk.
That timing works. I need one for myself and one for Elaine to look over before our Sunday call.
Elaine says you two are attacking the archive boxes Tuesday. Want me to haul the banker boxes down before you get here?
Please put the two labeled Norwich 2012-2016 near the table. Those have the forms, transport notes, and payment logs.
Got it. Also saw an envelope with your name and four receipts from a Dr. Kline. Separate pile?
Yes, set that aside. That was from right after Mom's service, when I was trying to keep the rest of it orderly.
Elaine says you skipped Bruins highlights for another lunch screen thing. Must have been a good one.
It was useful in places. The speaker showed why the black-box estimates looked clean but drifted badly in the last decade of withdrawals.
Sounds like a boat gauge that works until fog rolls in.
Exactly. I stripped my sheet back to plain withdrawal rates and two stress cases.
Elaine says you have a spreadsheet for the furnace and roof stuff. Mine is an envelope and a bad memory.
Mine is plain: monthly pulls into separate lines for roof, car, insurance, and medical. It keeps repairs from touching the 8-month cushion.
That is more disciplined than my system. I find the bill when it bites me.
The trick is making it boring. Same day each month, before I think about any extra work money.
That old impeller chart you sent was dead on. Yard guy said the 1978 sheet still matches the housing.
Good. Dad marked those charts by hand whenever a part number changed. I copied the margin notes before the paper got brittle.
Elaine says you also labeled the photo sleeves by who typed the cards. That is a level of order I do not possess.
The initials matter. Her old typing cards use the same two-letter marks as the counter slips, so it helps keep the dates straight.
Weather looks sloppy Saturday. If we skip the club workday, your 1 p.m. Foxborough spreadsheet may get more attention than the bilge pump.
The pump is more predictable. I still want to see what they do with the line and the secondary.
A rational man would wait for camp. Engineers and New England sports people rarely qualify.
Fair enough. I will bring the socket set if the rain holds off.
Saw your note about the retirement model misbehaving. Did you want diner math or just a second set of eyes?
Second set of eyes. I nearly wrote a long post about it, then decided a booth and coffee would do less damage.
Wise. Engineers have been ruining simple designs with public drafts since steam power.
Saturday at 9:30 then. I will bring the printout, not the drama.
Read the book chapter you sent. The author is annoyingly patient, but the housing math is solid.
Solid math earns patience. I underlined the part where he separates what he can prove from what he merely wants.
You also slipped a postcard in there. That a bridge sketch?
A quick one from the Thames walk. It kept the margin notes from becoming only objections.
I found the small installation photo you asked about. It is from the corner near the blue chairs.
Thank you. I saved the MFA story with the window shadows and wanted to compare the spacing before I forgot.
That comparison makes sense. I will be in the New London space until 5 if you want a second look before I change that corner.
Elaine says not to fuss for Sunday. I can bring rolls.
Rolls would help. I already set chicken aside and will use the rosemary branches before they get woody.
Good. I will stay out of the kitchen and talk Bruins.
I tagged you in the installation photographs, but only if you want them on your timeline. The light on the stairwell came through beautifully.
Thank you. I saved the photos and may send them privately to Elaine. I keep the public page spare.
Understood. Also, ignore the caption debate under the gallery post. It has wandered far from the work.
I saw enough. If someone asks about the building dates, I will point them to the archive entry, not the thread.
Wind is clean by 1100, ugly by 1400. I would take the early slot and leave the committee coffee untouched.
Agreed. I will check the notice board before we rig anything.
Bring that Thames photo Elaine mentioned. I want to see whether the crane in the background is the older Stothert type.
I can bring it. The crane and the mud at low water are the parts I remember best.
I read the packet you marked up. Your margin notes are very you: where is the baseline, who checks the footage, what changed after training.
If a department buys cameras and new classes, the public ought to see more than a purchase order.
You also circled the dispatch chart three times. Engineers do enjoy arrows.
Only because the chart separates calls that need a badge from calls that need a nurse and a van.
Your spreadsheet contraption survive quarter-end, or did the new helper invent a column again?
It suggested a clean summary, but I kept the original query and notebook cells in the appendix. Useful draft, not evidence.
Good. Machines are allowed to sharpen pencils. They do not get to sign the drawing.
Exactly. The deck will show a range and the two drivers we can actually trace.
The genealogy site wants a place tag for you. Should I use Norwich for the 1962 entry or leave it broader?
Use Norwich. Elaine has the clerk copy, so that is the cleanest source.
Got it. Also, the benefits form screenshot you sent has a line for discharge paperwork. I marked it N/A unless you object.
That is right. I never had papers of that kind to misplace.
Still okay if I crash there Friday? I can take the back room if it is not buried.
Mom sent me scans from the Norwich box. Wild how direct those old notes are. No glossary needed, just that impossible penmanship.
You can. I need to shift the stack of railway books, the Cinque Terre notebook, and one unfinished hull off the narrow bed.
That was the house: plain talk, formal handwriting, and someone saving every program from the old green.
If I crash there after Providence on the 28th, is the small room usable or still stacked with your city books?
Usable. I moved the Florence, Porto, and Quebec stacks to the top shelf and left the desk clear.
No rush. I can work around clamps if the Wi-Fi reaches the desk.
Are you going back there next Sunday or was that a one-off with Mom?
Nice. Also send me the thing you wrote on port taxes and those train stations when you are ready.
It reaches. The two monitors are on the other wall, and I will keep the basil pots out of your bag's path.
Probably a one-off for now. I go when family timing makes sense, not on a schedule.
I am tightening it tonight. It pulls from one five-day block and one Friday-Monday run, so the dates need to be right.
Mom said you're still the only person who knows what was in all those folders from Grandma and Grandpa. That sounds like a second job.
It felt like one: signatures, account statements, rides, appointment calendars, then repeat the next month.
Did you just muscle through it, or did you have any outside help keeping yourself level?
Briefly. A few appointments after your grandmother died. Useful enough that I still tell people not to be stubborn about it.
The Marston watercolors are hung now. The small harbor piece you liked in the preview reads much better in afternoon light.
I can stop in at 5:00. If you are closing near 6:30, I can take the little table at On the Waterfront afterward.
That timing is civilized. I will join for one course if the installation checklist behaves.
Good. I will keep it modest and make Sunday a blank page.
A collector from Greenwich asked whether my price schedule was too conservative. I almost wished you were here with one of your neat little risk grids.
Those grids started in lecture halls and got refined on client statements, not in galleries. Send the numbers if you like.
I will. Also, your note about choosing a local book of clients over a louder New York room would fit the exhibition essay better than you think.
Only if you leave out the part where I wore one decent suit until the cuffs gave up.
Before our call tomorrow, do you still want me to save the blue town envelope? Robert almost recycled it.
Please save it. I want to compare the wording with the newspaper endorsements before I mail mine.
I will put it by the phone. I also found Dad's old Mystic Seaport booklet in the same drawer.
Keep that out too. I have been meaning to look at the pier photographs after I finish the morning quotes.
Elaine says you were still at the keys late Thursday. That old cabinet must still have some fight in it.

Thank you. I will add them to the family binder after I compare the dates with the service-log pages.

I will. Please do not let every helpful person become another standing obligation.
Good. Please do not make supper out of crackers at the desk again.
That is why I am writing limits first and names second. The cash line is already set aside.

Before Sunday, could you remind me how you keep the dental and medical cards sorted? Robert has three envelopes on the table.

Thank you. That sounds simple enough. Please do not let the office keep you too late again.
I should be done by 5:45 if the last review is clean. Then I will call.
You still use that Saturday spreadsheet? I am trying to make one that doesn't make me hate opening it.

Did the rain kill your loop today, or are you still doing the stubborn uncle thing?

That is more organized than half my office.

Good timing. I skipped the new lens and put that money into the coastal account instead.
Sensible trade. The pad will suit those narrow lanes and angled windows better than a camera anyway.
Please hold it for me until Tuesday. I want to test whether the paper handles quick shadows.
I saved you a seat for Thursday's gallery talk, but I saw the city packet in your tote and guessed you might be cross-referencing tables instead.

That sounds less elegant than the new sculpture, though probably more consequential.
Maybe. I also want to compare it with the small stack I know personally: my two road stops and Mrs. Keane's car-window report.

Good. Mine still shows the same April line, so I will leave it alone. I only wanted to be sure after the redistricting notice.

That sounds very organized. I am glad you keep a cushion before helping me sort Robert's bills.
I saw another awful post about ballots being thrown out. I did not share it.
I keep enough aside for small surprises first. Paperwork is easier when nothing is pressing on the door.
Wise. The town site has the actual cure rules. I printed those, plus the sewer-rate sheet, before Sunday's call.

Are you still coming Sunday around four, or would you rather I call after supper?
That would have pleased Dad. He inspected them before we left for the photographer.
Four is fine. I plan to walk by the river earlier, then roast the salmon and use whatever dill survived the cold night.
Mum's handwriting on the back says Norwich, June 1978, and she called me 'little E.' I had forgotten that.
Cover the pots if it drops again. My basil looked offended this morning!
I remember. You were standing on the lower step so the four of us would fit in the frame.
I moved the basil closer to the wall. The rosemary never complains.

Sunday at 4 is still ours by phone. I have Martin at the club tomorrow morning and Janet and Paul for lunch Monday, so I am keeping Sunday quiet.

Short would be fine. I am taking Paul to the place with the decent Chianti by the glass on Monday.
Will Sunday at four still work, or are you buried in those end-of-month files again?
Four works. I have one workbook, one database pull, and a review note left before I close the laptop.

I won't. The note says which items are checked and which ones are just directional.
North wind is tolerable by 9. Shoreline walk first, diner after?
Saturday wind looks tolerable by ten. Diner after, or are you preserving the sacred afternoon silence?
Yes. I need five minutes at the bench to jot the cuff numbers, then coffee.
Diner is fine if we keep it early. I have the house exactly in working order and would rather end the day there.
Diner has oatmeal. Their hash is engineered for regret.
Efficient system. I will not argue with a man who knows where every saucepan lives.
Oatmeal it is. I already packed the pill sleeve, so no detour home.
Wind is wrong for tomorrow. I am declaring the boat wiser than us.
That is the advantage. No committee moves the pans.

That sounds like a punishment designed by an accountant with a harpsichord.
Possibly. I also have Clara's catalog waiting, so the afternoon will be less stern.

Agreed. The version after those two online talks is calmer: baseline, bad sequence, long-life case.
Good. Engineering rule: remove the clever part first and see if the bridge still stands.

Good. Models behave better when the exciting number is not treated as the new baseline.
That is the idea. I only revisit the base once the cash reserve is still sitting near eight months after the transfers.
Tuesday looks dry enough for the harbor walk. Assuming you are not buried under municipal paperwork again.
Only a small stack: April packet, Mrs. Alvarez's state confirmation, and two receipts I need to put with the March card statement.
Receipts from the forum groups?
Yes. $25 and $30. The body-camera ordinance discussion was more useful than I expected.
Wind finally dropped. Avery Point looked tolerable when I drove past.
I went after the consulting call. One hard lap by the water, no podcast.
Elegant system: fewer inputs, better output.
Exactly. Came home quieter, and the cuff has been kinder this month.

Plain enough. Tea and a hot shower can stay in the comfort department.
Exactly. Comfort is useful. The schedule should come from the people with your chart.

No danger of that. I checked the agenda and closed Facebook.
Good. Bruins at 8. Cleaner use of your evening.
Agreed. Send me the score if I miss the first period.

Mother's side was better at saving church slips. Father's Whitcomb folder is mostly town copies and clipped notices.

events.notes: Ask about Robert's paperwork folder and whether Andrew is still coming through Providence station before Easter.

events.title: Walk, cuff log, pill case
events.notes: Record morning numbers before leaving. Refill Tuesday/Saturday slots. Pick up plain oats and roasted almonds afterward.

events.title: Community Center belt
events.notes: Brisk pace only. Enter cuff numbers and night graph after breakfast.

events.title: River walk before forecast deck
events.notes: Shoes by door. Finish before 8:15 client numbers review. No spreadsheet edits after dinner.

events.title: Monthly transfer check
events.notes: Confirm checking sweep ran: 401k, IRA, brokerage, HSA. Refill roof/car/travel buckets. Keep base checking at 8.0x monthly spend before moving any March variable pay.

events.title: Office: month-close signoffs and staff reviews
events.notes: Bring laptop dock. Approve variance packet by 10:30, meet with Nina and Omar after lunch, HR portal reminder due before leaving.

events.title: February worksheet closeout
events.notes: Reconcile 13,300 top line against 8,000 landed. Move small surplus to rainy-day account after utilities clear. File $0 statements with tax folder.

events.title: 65 worksheet: hours, clients, reserve line
events.notes: Update rows for current retainers, 2-day ceiling, intro names, and months of expenses left untouched. Freeze assumptions before changing totals.

events.title: Italy folder: fare watch + small transfer
events.notes: Move $175 after consulting deposit clears. Compare September fares into Pisa and Genoa. Mark Vernazza overlook, Manarola stairs, and train times in notebook.

events.title: Dr. Hsu portal call: March questions
events.notes: Ask about timing for the left-arm pharmacy appointment. Bring printed CDC age table and CT town health office notice. Leave the Nextdoor thread out of the folder. Mention shoulder stretches and Thursday massage only as comfort items.

events.title: Town Hall / library errand loop
events.location: Norwich Town Hall, then Otis Library
events.notes: Registrar counter: confirm April 14 address card. Library scanner: Mrs. Alvarez packet, 1099-R, SSA-1099, property tax credit worksheet. File two $25 email receipts from CT Justice Center and Harbor Forum.

events.title: Town clerk counter: enrollment card and April primary cutoff
events.location: Norwich City Hall, 100 Broadway, Norwich, CT
events.notes: Bring license. Do not change line choice unless the fiscal slate changed since the sample ballot. Ask about absentee form dates.

events.title: House reset after Andrew
events.notes: Wash spare sheets, put extra mug back on top shelf, set thermostat back to weekday setting, soup portion from freezer.

events.title: March forecast refresh
events.notes: Open workbook v7, rerun warehouse query, update notebook output, add one paragraph on assumptions before sharing deck.

events.title: Noon webcast: model risk in portfolio income tools
events.notes: Join from saved professional-network link. Compare notes with March drawdown workbook; avoid adding the new forecast tab until checked.

events.title: Public safety budget listening session
events.notes: Ask about quarterly dashboard: stop totals, complaint outcomes, camera-release log, training hours, and crisis-team pilot results. Bring folder with the two Route 2 slips and Mrs. Keane's driveway glass report as examples of ordinary records being hard to track.

events.title: Clara opening, then Thames Landing

events.notes: Check the west-wall prints. Ask at dinner whether the Rioja is offered by the glass. Keep Friday morning unscheduled.

events.title: Stop & Shop run, portion containers

events.title: Retirement model pass, source checks, then gallery stop

events.notes: Print assumptions page. Mark unsupported cells. Leave laptop at home for Clara's 11:20 opening and use blue pocket notebook.

events.title: Harbor roster: launch key and spring line check

events.title: Clara - Water Street new show

events.title: Coffee, keyboard, Sunday papers

events.title: Clear south window bench; basil, thyme, sanding block

events.title: Sort back-room shelf: Rome, Lisbon, Montreal

events.title: Check Foxborough notes before free agency opens
